newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes up 38 cts on U.S. storm worry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes up 38 cts on U.S. storm worry.

text.p: IPE Brent closed 38 cents higher in line with stronger NYMEX futures on Thursday on the threat of storm disruption to oil production in the Gulf of Mexico.
Front month September last traded up 38 cents at $18.68 a barrel, having peaked at $18.79 two hours before the close.
Dealers said the IPE contract came off the highs after front month NYMEX WTI failed to breach key resistance at $20.24 a barel.

Dealers said the storm was the most important of a flurry of bullish headlines that pushed values up but the market still faced a sobering array of bearish background factors that are likely to feature strongly next week.
"Clearly it was the storm concerns that took it up today but I can't help feeling we'll be going all the way back down next week," one broker said.
"Unless there are any further problems in the Gulf coast from this particular storm I can't see prices getting any higher," a dealer said.
Iraq is poised to sell big volumes of oil next month, Germany is to sell oil from stocks and North Sea loadings are not going to be hit by oilfield maintenance.
Brent has traded between $18.96 and $17.32 for over a month and some dealers see the range holding.
Dealers said the Brent cargo market was also firmer after talk a U.S. refiner had chartered a ULCC to take Brent transatlantic.
Oil products were also firm in Europe, helping support Brent. Light ends of the barrel were up $4 a tonne bouyed by gains of nearly 2 cents a gallon on the NYMEX and strong naphtha demand in Asia.
August gas oil ended $3.25 a tonne higher at $167.
